SMTO-TSK-0017 — Task intent changed

GUID: ed16d51e-c9fa-4be4-a4e6-199565005b7a
Slug: task-intent-changed
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • What the task was asked to do changed after this action was prepared, for example by a steering message or an edited queued prompt. SMTO didn't apply the older version, so the task can follow your latest instructions.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page and read the task's latest reply, including any steering messages or edited queued prompt. This shows which version of your instructions SMTO already accepted.
  2. If the task is paused or waiting, select Resume or Continue task on its latest reply. Continuing from the latest state lets the task work on the updated request instead of the old one.
  3. If you want to change the instructions again, type them as a new message rather than resending an earlier one. A new message is treated as a new request, so it can't clash with the instructions already recorded.

What success looks like

  • The task continues and its next reply reflects your latest instructions.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend an old message or queued prompt to force it through; that is what this check prevents.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The action was built on task intent that has since been superseded: a reused submission or steering ID is bound to different intent, a prepared queued task no longer matches its source, or pending amendments replaced the snapshot the action used.

What this means

  • A reused submission/steering identity has a different intent digest or run, a preparation differs from current execution intent, or pending amendments supersede the action's snapshot. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A reused submission/steering identity has a different intent digest or run, a preparation differs from current execution intent, or pending amendments supersede the action's snapshot.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the original accepted intent/digest and pending amendments; an existing identity cannot be reassigned to changed work.

How to fix it

  • The intent digest for the reused submission or amendment ID differs from the one already recorded, or the queued task's Task Contract was prepared from an earlier source. Reload the run, reconcile the original submission, and resume or resubmit the new intent through the current controls with a fresh identity; never resend the old identity with changed content.
  • Resume through the current controls to address the updated accepted request and existing evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The original submission is reconciled and distinct new intent is accepted through its supported flow.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
